claims.justification: Roary pan-genomes of 26–27 genomes span 26,839–48,118 genes and the Clade-1 accumulation rises monotonically to 15,247, which is qualitatively consistent with a very large pan-genome but does not directly reach the paper’s ~60,000 estimate from much larger sampling.

The paper’s ~600 core genes were computed on the homogeneous BCSL_114 set using HaMStR, whereas the replication used Roary on different genome sets and thresholds, so the specific core-gene claim is not directly testable here.

FastANI shows a wide but coherent range across the group (median 91.8%, range 79.9–100%) with B. anthracis vs B. cereus s.s. mean 96.25%, supporting a genomically cohesive yet structured B. cereus s.l. cluster.

B. anthracis strains are near-clonal by ANI (99.99–100.0% within anthracis) and show very high similarity to some B. cereus s.s. genomes (max 99.98%), consistent with anthracis being nested within cereus diversity.

Within the Clade-1 subset, core-gene and accessory trees are concordant and show anthracis collapsing into a near-zero-branch clade intermingled with cereus/thuringiensis (no clean monophyly), but the evidence provided does not explicitly demonstrate recovery of three major clades across the full species set.
Pan-genome accumulation for Clade-1 remains strongly increasing with no saturation (the 17th genome still adds ~492 new genes), supporting an open pan-genome.

overall_justification: Key qualitative conclusions about genomic cohesion/structure, anthracis clonality and nesting, open pan-genome behavior, and concordant core/accessory signal are supported, while the specific HaMStR-derived core-gene count and full three-clade system are not directly reproduced with the smaller/different dataset and methods.
